qa.name: Lumbrical 1
qa.origin: Lateral side of the tendon of flexor digitorum profundus to the index finger
qa.insertion: Lateral band of the extensor expansion of the index finger
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint and extension of the interphalangeal joints of the index finger
qa.clinical_note: Lumbricals 1 and 2 are innervated by the median nerve; lumbricals 3 and 4 are innervated by the ulnar nerve — unique muscles that arise from and modulate their own antagonist

qa.name: Lumbrical 2
qa.origin: Lateral side of the tendon of flexor digitorum profundus to the middle finger
qa.insertion: Lateral band of the extensor expansion of the middle finger
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint and extension of the interphalangeal joints of the middle finger
qa.clinical_note: Innervated by the median nerve along with lumbrical 1 — median nerve injury causes clawing of the index and middle fingers because these lumbricals are lost

qa.name: Lumbrical 3
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus to the middle and ring fingers
qa.insertion: Lateral band of the extensor expansion of the ring finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint and extension of the interphalangeal joints of the ring finger
qa.clinical_note: Innervated by the ulnar nerve along with lumbrical 4 — ulnar nerve injury causes more pronounced clawing of the ring and little fingers because these lumbricals are lost

qa.name: Lumbrical 4
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus to the ring and little fingers
qa.insertion: Lateral band of the extensor expansion of the little finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint and extension of the interphalangeal joints of the little finger
qa.clinical_note: Ulnar nerve injury causes ulnar claw hand — more pronounced in ring and little fingers because lumbricals 3 and 4 are lost; median nerve injury causes a milder claw in index and middle

qa.name: Dorsal Interosseous 1
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the first and second metacarpals
qa.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the index finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the index finger away from the middle finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: DAB — Dorsal interossei ABduct fingers from the midline of the middle finger; all four dorsal interossei are innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve

qa.name: Dorsal Interosseous 2
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the second and third metacarpals
qa.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the middle finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the middle finger toward the index finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: The middle finger has two dorsal interossei — dorsal interosseous 2 abducts it toward the index finger and dorsal interosseous 3 abducts it toward the ring finger

qa.name: Dorsal Interosseous 3
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the third and fourth metacarpals
qa.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the middle finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the middle finger toward the ring finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: Along with dorsal interosseous 2 allows the middle finger to spread in both directions — spreading all fingers apart tests all four dorsal interossei simultaneously

qa.name: Dorsal Interosseous 4
qa.origin: Adjacent sides of the fourth and fifth metacarpals
qa.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the ring finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the ring finger away from the middle finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: Wasting of the dorsal interossei visible as hollowing between the metacarpals on the dorsum of the hand is a classic sign of ulnar nerve palsy

qa.name: Palmar Interosseous 1
qa.origin: Medial side of the second metacarpal
qa.insertion: Medial base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the index finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Adduction of the index finger toward the middle finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: PAD — Palmar interossei ADduct fingers toward the midline of the middle finger; tested by asking the patient to grip a piece of paper between adjacent fingers

qa.name: Palmar Interosseous 2
qa.origin: Lateral side of the fourth metacarpal
qa.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the ring finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Adduction of the ring finger toward the middle finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: All palmar interossei are innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve — loss causes inability to adduct fingers and contributes to the claw hand deformity

qa.name: Palmar Interosseous 3
qa.origin: Lateral side of the fifth metacarpal
qa.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx and extensor expansion of the little finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Adduction of the little finger toward the middle finger, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint, extension of the interphalangeal joints
qa.clinical_note: Remember DAB and PAD — Dorsal interossei ABduct, Palmar interossei ADduct; the middle finger has no palmar interosseous as it is the axis of hand movement

qa.name: Palmaris Brevis
qa.innervation: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Wrinkles the skin of the hypothenar eminence, deepens the hollow of the palm, protects the ulnar nerve and artery in Guyon canal
qa.clinical_note: Only intrinsic hand muscle innervated by the superficial branch of the ulnar nerve — its contraction is preserved in deep ulnar nerve lesions helping to localize the level of injury
